correctness.rationale: Exact bijection between all representations and nonnegative height/coefficient pairs yields cost formula C_h,z; monotonicity C_{h+1}>=C_h holds for every a>=2, so min(C1,C0+3 when available) is exactly the second distinct representation cost. The residue threshold formulas follow, as do max-and-sum invariants. Period-four polynomial simplification is derived by explicit floor and residue sums; 12 smaller a computed by substitution of the proved formula. Finite capped-denumerant DP independently checks every residue for a=2..400.

originality.rationale: The original 2022 shifted-square paper gives the classical zero-representation invariant and does not assert first-repeat Apéry thresholds. The most relevant explicit p-Frobenius theorem applies only to arithmetic-progression triples, while (a,a+1,a+4) is nonarithmetic; general p-Apéry identities do not compute these residue thresholds. The conditional triple formula requires divisibilities absent for a>=14. Actual published-finding corpus queries found no claim implying this infinite-family classification among ranked nearby items. Incomplete bibliographic coverage is documented as a residual risk rather than a proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: The ranked semantic database retrieval is not an exhaustive theorem-equivalence search.
Unindexed earlier generalized Frobenius formulas or exact sequence tables could contain an equivalent closed form.
Some relevant published journal editions were not inspected independently of their accessible preprints.

value.rationale: First-repeat thresholds are a motivated next numerical-semigroup invariant beyond the classic shifted-square g0 literature, and knowledge of g0 does not determine them. The complete all-residue Apéry classification yields two exact infinite-family invariants, establishes a sharp quasipolynomial onset at a=14 and resolves the complete smaller-base table, not merely an arbitrary isolated computation. At \(a=13\), the eventual formula predicts \(g_1=102\) but the proved threshold yields \(g_1=89\), so the uniform starting bound \(a=14\) cannot be decreased.
